blocks.task_summary: Sketch y = log2 x, y = log10 x, and y = x on the same axes with correct domain, asymptotes, concavity, relative positions, and x-intercept at (1,0).
method_path: Sketch y = log2 x with domain x > 0, vertical asymptote x = 0, concave-down shape
Sketch y = log10 x with same domain, asymptote, and concavity
Show correct relative positions: log2 above log10 for x > 1, log2 below log10 for 0 < x < 1
Indicate x-intercept at (1, 0) for both log graphs
Sketch y = x as a straight line through origin with gradient 1

evidence.basis: clearly labelled graphs of y=log2 x and y=log10 x with correct domain, asymptotic behaviour and concavity evident A1; correct relative positions of the two log graphs both above and below the x-axis A1; (1,0) indicated (coordinates not required) A1; correct graph of y=x A1

blocks.task_summary: Use calculus to find the minimum value of x - ln x, justifying it is a minimum.
method_path: Differentiate: d/dx(x - ln x) = 1 - 1/x
Set derivative to zero: 1 - 1/x = 0, solve to get x = 1
Evaluate expression at x = 1: 1 - ln 1 = 1
Find second derivative: d2/dx2 = 1/x2
Note 1/x2 > 0 for all x > 0, confirming minimum
Conclude minimum value is 1
accepted_alternatives: Use first-derivative sign test: for 0 < x < 1, derivative negative; for x > 1, derivative positive; hence minimum at x = 1

evidence.basis: d/dx(x-ln x) = 1-1/x A1; attempts to solve derivative = 0 for x (M1); when x=1, x-ln x=1 A1; d/dx(1-1/x)=1/x2 A1; 1/x2 > 0 (when x=1) R1; hence x-ln x has a minimum value of 1

blocks.task_summary: Hence deduce that x > ln x for all positive x.
method_path: From part (b), x - ln x >= 1 > 0 for all x in R+
Rearrange: x > ln x
accepted_alternatives: State x - ln x > 0, hence x > ln x

evidence.basis: EITHER x-ln x >= 1 (x in R+) R1 OR x-ln x > 0 (x in R+) R1; THEN so x > ln x AG

blocks.task_summary: By investigating graphs, write down the number of intersection points p, q, r for three intervals of a.
method_path: Investigate y = loga x against y = x for 0 < a < 1: graphs intersect once, so p = 1
Investigate for 1 < a < 1.4: graphs intersect twice, so q = 2
Investigate for 1.5 < a < 2: graphs do not intersect, so r = 0

evidence.basis: Table: Interval 0<a<1, Number of intersection points p=1; 1<a<1.4, q=2; 1.5<a<2, r=0. Note: Award A1 for p=1, A2 for q=2 and A1 for r=0.

blocks.task_summary: Find the exact coordinates of the tangency point P where y = x is tangent to y = loga x, and the exact value of a, for 1.4 <= a <= 1.5.
method_path: Differentiate: d/dx(loga x) = 1/(x ln a)
Set derivative equal to slope of y = x: 1/(x ln a) = 1
Obtain x = 1/ln a
At tangency point, loga x = x, so loga(1/ln a) = 1/ln a
Rewrite using change of base: ln(1/ln a)/ln a = 1/ln a, hence ln(1/ln a) = 1
Solve: 1/ln a = e, so x = e
Coordinates of P: (e, e)
Solve for a: ln a = 1/e, so a = e^(1/e)
accepted_alternatives: METHOD 2: solve loga(1/ln a) = 1/ln a for a first to get a = e^(1/e), then find x = e and P = (e, e)
METHOD 3: write tangent line equation y = [1/(x1 ln a)](x - x1) + loga(x1), equate to y = x, solve for x1 = e, then find a = e^(1/e)

evidence.basis: d/dx(loga x)=1/(x ln a) A1; attempts to solve 1/(x ln a)=1 for x (M1); x=1/ln a A1; attempts to solve loga x = x at x=1/ln a (M1); x=e; coordinates of P are (e,e) A1A1; attempts to solve for a analytically (M1); a=e^(1/e) A1

blocks.task_summary: Write the exact set of a values for which the graphs have two intersection points.
method_path: State: 1 < a < e^(1/e)

evidence.basis: (i) 1 < a < e^(1/e) A1. Note: Award A0 for a < e^(1/e).

blocks.task_summary: Write the exact set of a values for which the graphs have no intersection points.
method_path: State: a > e^(1/e)

evidence.basis: (ii) a > e^(1/e) A1. Note: Only award FT for 1.4 <= a <= 1.5. If a not exact, award at most A0A1 in part (f) for consistent approximate endpoint value.
